blocks.task_summary: Find the area completely enclosed by the curves y = e^x, y = -e^x, and the lines x = -1 and x = 1.
method_path: Set up integral of (e^x - (-e^x)) = 2e^x from x=-1 to x=1
accepted_alternatives: Integrate e^x from -1 to 1 and -e^x from -1 to 1 separately, then subtract: (e - e^{-1}) - (-(e - e^{-1})) = 2(e - e^{-1})

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: attempt to set up integral (e^x - (-e^x)) = 2e^x or e^x and then double (M1); ∫(e^x - (-e^x))dx OR 2∫e^x dx; = 2∫_{-1}^{1} e^x dx; = 2[e^x]_{-1}^{1} (A1); attempt to substitute correct limits into their integrated function and subtract (M1); = 2(e - 1/e), 2e - 2/e, 2e - 2e^{-1} A1. METHOD 2: ∫_{-1}^{1} e^x dx = [e^x]_{-1}^{1} and ∫_{-1}^{1} -e^x dx = [-e^x]_{-1}^{1} (A1); attempt to substitute correct limits into both their integrated functions and subtract (M1); = e - e^{-1} and -(e^{-1} - e); subtracts their two integrals in correct order (M1); = (e - e^{-1}) - (-(e - e^{-1})) = 2(e - 1/e), 2e - 2/e, 2e - 2e^{-1} A1.
